note: Where a candidate for a town, township or county seat files, and how a visit there is kept. Which government runs local elections comes from each state's municipal election rule pack; the five territories, which have no such pack, are read here. Office hours, the visit's length and the clerk's title are estimates until a place's own are read.

officeHours.estimatedFrom: Weekday business hours county and municipal clerks' offices commonly keep, 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday through Friday

visitMinutes.estimatedFrom: The time a counter visit takes to ask about a seat and complete a declaration of candidacy

journey.basis: The same authored local journey the community room uses; no street geography is implied

PR.estimatedFrom: Puerto Rico's State Elections Commission (Comisión Estatal de Elecciones) conducts the island's elections, municipal legislatures included

GU.estimatedFrom: The Guam Election Commission conducts every election on Guam

VI.estimatedFrom: The Virgin Islands Board of Elections conducts every election in the territory

AS.estimatedFrom: The American Samoa Election Office conducts every election in the territory

MP.estimatedFrom: The Commonwealth Election Commission conducts every election in the Northern Mariana Islands

filingOfficers.note: Who receives a local candidate's filing papers, read from each state's election code for the 33 states whose local elections a county office runs (read October 8, 2026). municipal.level says whether a town's own officer or the county's takes a town seat's filing; a null title means the town's own clerk, or for a county the county clerk. States not listed file with the town's own clerk, as their administration rule says. body marks a board or commission rather than one officer; counterTitle names the official who takes filings at its counter (read October 8, 2026); a board with no such title read has the town's own clerk at the counter.
